Voice-Based
Meal Verification

Natural student ID and name recordings, classical DSP, and a conservative rule for serving the right student.

Group 07 · Hall dining system · Project v4.1.4

MATLAB 2024a · 2026-09-27 09:34:12

← → to navigate · M for reading mode · N for speaker notes

Open the separate DSP Theory Manual

Speaker note

Our objective is accurate meal verification. Wrong-student acceptance matters more than avoiding a retry. The project extends the supplied MATLAB system and preserves natural speech.

ID first, name only when needed

  1. Identify the account to verify

    The counter enters the seven-digit claimed student ID independently of voice ranking.

  2. Speak the complete ID

    Say “2206150” naturally in one utterance. No separate digit recording.

  3. Use name as a fallback

    If ID cannot verify the claim, say the full name once. Success ends voice verification immediately.

  4. Finish after this pair

    If name also fails, display FAILED. There is no automatic repeat of either phrase.

Each accepting phrase must pass

Candidate = entered claim
AND distance ≤ phrase ceiling
AND runner-up margin ≥ phrase floor

Recording ends after the detected pause, up to 8 seconds including the 0.5-second ambient profile. Payment, meal-window and duplicate checks follow voice verification.

MFCC/DTW compares acoustic templates. A match is evidence about the claimed identity; these trials do not separately measure literal phrase correctness.

Source: verify_meal_workflow.m · speaker_verification_decision.m · capture_voice_features.m

Speaker note

The typed ID identifies the account being tested and must never come from the winning voice label. Say ID once. Only after an ID failure is the full name requested once. If name also fails, the result is FAILED. Speech-end detection can stop each recording before the eight-second maximum.

Five proposed modifications

ModificationSenior description / legacy proxyOur implementationMeasured evidence and limits
1. Level and sampling44.1 kHz processing. The proposal describes no RMS AGC.RMS AGC and anti-alias polyphase conversion at 80/441 produce an 8 kHz DSP signal.Development genuine acceptance: 8 kHz 100.0%; 44.1 kHz 77.4%. Compute comparison follows.
2. Liveness heuristicNo replay gate in the proposal-described senior system.Compare DFT energy in 20–200 Hz with 20–3800 Hz after speech detection.Implemented band-energy ratio. No labeled phone-replay trial establishes its detection accuracy.
3. Ambient noiseStatic pre-emphasis: 1 − 0.97z⁻¹, also present in the legacy scripts.Estimate 0.5 s of ambient noise and subtract its power spectrum with a floor. Retain signal phase.Synthetic mean SNR change 5.38 dB across 372 perturbations. Real cafeteria-babble gain remains unmeasured.
4. Speech boundariesEnergy-only endpoints in the available legacy scripts.Adaptive STE plus a two-sided ZCR band, short-gap bridging and brief-run removal.Synthetic non-speech false triggers: energy 1/4, hybrid 0/4. Field performance unmeasured.
5. Dining operationsHall-entry workflow without meal-specific rules.datetime-based meal windows and a CSV record keyed by student, date and meal.The component regression records repeat refusal and next-window allowance. Concurrent-counter correctness remains untested.

Development-selected DSP variant: current_dsp. Deployment values come directly from its separate security audit.

distance = accumulated DTW cost / (N + M)
margin = runner-up distance / best distance

Selection first minimizes accepted false claims, then genuine rejections. The candidate and operating points are frozen before final-split feature extraction. An outside-threshold runner-up never waives the margin requirement.

An ID success needs no name recording. When ID fails, name must independently select the claim and pass its own distance and margin gates. A tie, invalid distance or missing meaningful competition cannot verify the claim.

FAR / false-claim WSAR = accepted wrong claims ÷ false claims. FRR = rejected genuine claims ÷ genuine claims. Closed-set WSAR counts speakers with any accepted wrong claim, once per speaker. Top-1 is raw ID-candidate accuracy for fallback mode; successful name fallback does not change this ID diagnostic.

A 0% observed FAR means no false acceptances in these trials. It does not guarantee rejection of an unseen speaker, same-content impersonation or a replay.

Sampling and level control

Polyphase rate conversion

8,000 / 44,100 = 80 / 441

Anti-alias FIR filtering protects the 4 kHz folding boundary. A fixed duration contains 81.86% fewer samples at 8 kHz than at 44.1 kHz.

Time-based frame hops preserve approximately the same DTW frame count. Sample reduction is an arithmetic fact, not a measured end-to-end speedup.

The rate conversion reduces samples and per-frame FFT work. Recognition still determines whether that tradeoff is acceptable. AGC controls signal level but does not remove noise or establish physical distance robustness.

Ambient noise suppression

Each capture starts with an ambient profile. The STFT estimates mean noise power across that interval and subtracts it from each frame.

P̂speech = max(Pinput − 2Pnoise, 0.02Pnoise)

Reconstruction keeps the measured phase and uses weighted overlap-add. A stationary Wiener option is included as an experiment.

Nonstationary competing speech can change after the pre-roll. These experiments do not establish cafeteria-babble cancellation.

Gap bridging preserves short pauses. Brief-run removal filters isolated events. The energy-only experiment uses the current endpoint implementation with its ZCR gate disabled.

It is a controlled current-code ablation. The synthetic harmonic interval supplies known boundaries. Real speech, plates, fans and background conversations still require labeled field recordings.

Source: synthetic_vad_results.csv · hybrid_endpoint_detect.m

Speaker note

ZCR adds useful information to energy, but it cannot universally identify speech. Explain which synthetic fixtures changed and acknowledge that short-run removal also contributes to impulse rejection.

Sub-200 Hz liveness is a diagnostic heuristic

r = energy(20–200 Hz) / energy(20–3800 Hz)
62final archive recordings inspected
0.00035–0.58329observed low-band ratio range
0heuristic rejections in diagnostics

Welch-style averaging estimates the spectrum across detected speech. Too little low-frequency energy or excessive rumble causes rejection under the configured bounds.

No labeled live-versus-phone-replay corpus is available. These ratios do not provide replay FAR, replay detection accuracy, or a security guarantee.

Phone frequency response, the speaker’s pitch, room acoustics and microphone processing can overlap with this signal property. A real replay trial requires labeled captures through the actual loudspeaker and kiosk microphone.

Source: liveness_results.csv · check_liveness_lowfreq.m

Speaker note

Present this as the proposal's security heuristic and state its evidence limit clearly. A spectrum can show a low-band ratio. It cannot establish the physical origin of speech without a validated classification experiment.

A reproducible classroom demonstration

Live demonstration

  1. Launch the current entry point

    In MATLAB, open the project folder and run run_meal_system.

  2. Choose an enrolled account

    Enter its seven-digit ID. Wait for the ambient profile, then say the complete ID once. Recording ends after the detected pause. Say the name once only if prompted.

  3. Read the decision

    The accepting phrase must match the entered account and pass its distance and margin gates. Serving also needs payment, an open meal window, and no duplicate.

  4. Demonstrate failure

    Use a wrong claim with recordings that fail its gates. After one failed ID and one failed name, confirm FAILED and no meal served.

Safe preparation

Use a dedicated demonstration copy for meal/payment writes. Keep this evidence package and supplied student recordings unchanged.

Allow up to 8 seconds per phrase. Recording limits include the ambient pre-roll. Speaking time and compute time are different.

Expected distinctions

Verified means voice gates passed.
Served additionally means the business checks and meal log succeeded.
Retry leaves identity unconfirmed.

Source: run_meal_system.m · verify_meal_workflow.m · log_meal_csv.m

Speaker note

Before class, verify the microphone and use a disposable copy for business transactions. Never call a prerecorded-file regression a live demonstration. Show both the biometric verdict and the serving result.

Supplemental experiment: cross-correlation and DTW alignment

Four synthetic scalar feature sequences compare each query with its intended reference and one different event pattern. Both methods receive the same sequences. Cross-correlation searches the full range of global shifts; this supplemental DTW uses an unconstrained band and the project’s N+M normalization.

Timing conditionMatcherReference distanceDifferent distanceBest candidate
Identical timingCross-correlation00.640731Reference
Identical timingDTW00.302632Reference
Global shiftCross-correlation00.640731Reference
Global shiftDTW00.302632Reference
Uniform slowingCross-correlation0.6785880.522116Different pattern
Uniform slowingDTW00.289474Reference
Uneven timingCross-correlation0.4499810.396128Different pattern
Uneven timingDTW00.304878Reference

Both matchers rank the intended reference first for identical timing and a global shift. In these constructed slowing and uneven-timing cases, cross-correlation ranks the different pattern first while DTW preserves the reference ranking. Cross-correlation uses one minus normalized correlation; DTW uses accumulated feature distance. Compare rankings within each method, not the magnitudes across methods. Values within floating-point roundoff of zero are displayed as zero.

This is a controlled alignment illustration using four synthetic queries and 16 query–template scores. It is not human-speaker accuracy, an execution of the unavailable senior implementation, or part of the frozen 31-student calibration. It does not show that DTW always wins on real recordings.

Experiment limitations (17 rows)
TopicStatusLimitation
Dataset sizelimited31 enrolled students; one recording per phrase per split. Same-session takes do not establish field accuracy.
Evaluation designretrospectiveTake1 enrollment, take2 development, take3 final; recordings were inspected previously, so final is not untouched prospective validation.
Archive preprocessinglimitedAll roles use enrol_template_features with archived-template preprocessing and lenient quality; clipped or cropped legacy audio may be retained. These are not live microphone accuracy measurements.
False claimslimitedImpostors speak their own ID/name and claim another enrolled student; same-content impersonation and unknown-speaker trials are unavailable.
Decision policydefinedMode ID+Name means ID-first fallback: try ID for the supplied claim, then independently gated Name if ID fails. Conflicting phrases may accept two different enumerated claims. MULTIPLE CLAIMS is one source-pair outcome, not a selected identity.
DenominatorsdefinedPer variant/split/mode: N genuine claims and N(N-1) false claims. FAR and WSAR divide wrong accepted claims by N(N-1); ClosedSetWrongAccepted counts actual students with at least one false claim accepted, and ClosedSetWSAR divides that count by N. CorrectClaimIdentityErrors is the separate no-reassignment invariant. Pair FAR/FRR ignores identity/margin gates and is reported separately.
Top-1 rankingdefinedTop1Accuracy is the raw usable ID best candidate for ID and ID-first fallback, and the raw usable Name best candidate for Name-only. Invalid evidence has no ranked candidate. This diagnostic ignores thresholds/margins and does not replace ID ranking when Name fallback succeeds.
Senior baselineunavailableOriginal senior source and matched evaluation data are absent. Energy-only mode is a current-code ablation, not a measured senior baseline.
Microphone distanceunavailableNo measured capture-distance labels. Synthetic scalar gains are not physical microphone distances.
Field noiseunavailableNo quiet/fan/cafeteria/background-speech/impact condition labels or clean reference. Field SNR and condition-specific accuracy are unavailable.
VAD ground truthunavailableArchived recordings have no speech-boundary annotations; speech detection, misses and truncation rates cannot be inferred. Separate synthetic fixtures have known boundaries.
Replay securityunavailableNo labeled live/replay captures. Low-frequency heuristic outputs are diagnostics and do not establish replay resistance.
Multi-template enrollmentsupplementalSeparate retrospective leave-one-take-out scores compare one vs two enrollment templates after final evaluation; they do not select deployed thresholds.
Historical recordingsdiagnostic onlyPrior unsaved live incidents cannot be reconstructed. Historical challenges are separate from any newly supplied VSD enrollment recordings.
Synthetic stresssynthetic onlyDeterministic gain, additive-noise and endpoint fixtures characterize controlled perturbations; they are not field-condition or replay evidence.
Timing scopelimitedMATLAB wall times exclude capture, disk I/O, GUI, network and business actions. ID+Name timing sums both separately measured utterances: the full fallback path, not expected latency when ID passes immediately. Repeats characterize compute variation, not new speakers.
DeploymentunchangedSelected experimental parameters are saved in results only; no deployed thresholds or student/business/audio files are changed.
